entity_noun: instance of production for another party

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} qualifies only if ALL of these conditions hold for it:

rules.text: At least one {{entity_noun}} can be identified from the text — goods the business makes, or production steps it carries out on goods, on behalf of a party other than itself.

children.text: A standing offer to produce to other parties' requirements identifies such production even where no individual customer is named.

rules.text: The text says something substantive about the identified {{entity_noun}} — describing an activity, arrangement, or dealing that involves it — rather than only naming it, listing it as a topic, or mentioning it in passing. Which party is involved is not this condition's subject; [CON-3] and [CON-4] decide that.

The identified {{entity_noun}} is undertaken to the other party's order: what is produced is fixed by that party's design, specification, or requirements, or the output is supplied for that party to offer as its own — rather than being a good this business offers on its own account.

children.text: Design, engineering, or manufacturability input from this business does not change whose order it is; production of the business's own design still qualifies when the output is made for and supplied to the commissioning party.

rules.text: It is this business that {{entity_relationships.third_person}} the identified {{entity_noun}} — in an operation it runs — rather than arranging, brokering, or reselling production performed by another party.

children.text: A business that has its own goods produced elsewhere is buying such production, not performing it.

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} is ruled out if ANY of these guards is violated by it. Ruling out one candidate does not settle the classification — another candidate may still qualify:

rules.text: The arrangement behind the identified {{entity_noun}} is only sought, planned, or being set up, or has been discontinued, rather than current and actual.
